title: Gallstones and Concomitant Gastric Helicobacter Pylori Infection
brief_summary: In this study, the presence of H.Pylori in the gallbladder mucosa of patients with symptomatic gallstones undergoing cholecystectomy was investigated. Concomitant H.Pylori infection of the gastric mucosa was also investigated to study the relationship of gastric H.Pylori infection to gallstones. It was hypothesized that H.Pylori infection of the gastric mucosa may have a role in the formation of gallstones.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with acute cholecystitis, cholangitis, biliary and hepatic tumors, Crohn's disease, and previous gastric surgery were not considered suitable for evaluation.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients undergoing ERCP (endoscopic retrograde cholangio-pancreatography) and patients who have received H.Pylori eradication treatment in the last 6 month were also excluded from the study.
study_population: Ninety-four patients with symptomatic gallstones undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy were enrolled for the study.
